challenger_routes.why_not_selected_or_selected: SELECTED: a previous guard already dropped the output path, but only by recognising an output VERB, and this sentence says 'save output_path R.json' with no 'to', so the guard never fired -- and nothing at all excluded the source root. challenger_routes.why_not_selected_or_selected: SELECTED: apply the gate that already exists to the fallback before it may report success. Two supporting defects were found by measuring the same family. (1) Template key order for the repair capabilities is output_path, source_root, test_argv, test_paths, and test_argv is derived FROM the test paths, so counting a derived argv as a competing claim cancelled the role against itself: exclusivity emptied a correct test_paths, the fallback then assigned every file in the sentence, source included. (2) That masking hid a second defect: _repo_paths only checks that a path RESOLVES under the root, so 'test command /usr/bin/python3 T' bound usr/bin/python3 as a test file and the adapter rejected it with FILE_INVALID. Both are fixed generally: an argv is not a claim, and a role list may only name files that exist.
